source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) cholera bulletins, situation reports, or surveillance summaries covering Haiti Q4 2024 (October–December 2024).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MSPP is the primary national public health authority for Haiti and the authoritative source for subnational cholera case, death, and hospitalization counts by département and commune. French-language bulletins are the primary format.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify PAHO/WHO Haiti cholera situation reports, epidemiological updates, or country office bulletins covering 2024-10-01 to 2024-12-31.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO Haiti Country Office and WHO regularly publish cholera situation reports with case and death counts disaggregated by département, often citing MSPP data. These are high-priority collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify UNICEF Haiti, UN OCHA Haiti, and MSF situation reports or humanitarian updates referencing cholera case counts and deaths in Haiti during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: UNICEF, OCHA, and MSF publish regular humanitarian situation reports for Haiti that include cholera surveillance data, often with subnational breakdowns and hospitalization figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Cholera and AWD Platform data, WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON), or WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record entries for Haiti cholera in Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO global platforms aggregate and independently validate national cholera data. These sources can serve as held-back validation against MSPP and PAHO collection records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify ProMED-mail, HealthMap, or GOARN alerts referencing Haiti cholera cases or deaths during October–December 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: ProMED and HealthMap provide independent early-warning signals and can validate or flag discrepancies in official case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints on Haiti cholera epidemiology, case definitions, or AWD surveillance methodology relevant to 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources clarify case definitions (suspected, probable, confirmed), count semantics (cumulative vs. incident), and Vibrio cholerae strain characteristics used in Haiti surveillance.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify structured databases (e.g., Global Health Observatory, HDX/Humanitarian Data Exchange, ECDC) with Haiti cholera time-series data for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases may provide machine-readable cholera counts for Haiti that can contextualize and cross-check extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news sources (Reuters, AP, Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) reporting on Haiti cholera outbreaks, case counts, or deaths during Q4 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may contain early outbreak signals, quotes from health officials, or case/death figures not yet reflected in official bulletins, particularly given Haiti's challenging reporting environment.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics (cumulative vs. weekly incident), unclear geographic scope (national vs. subnational), or validation leakage risk for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Haiti cholera reports frequently mix cumulative totals with weekly incident counts, and national aggregates may obscure subnational data. Human review is needed to resolve these ambiguities before extraction.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: MSPP (Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population) is the primary national authority for Haiti cholera surveillance. MSPP publishes weekly and monthly cholera bulletins (Bulletins Épidémiologiques) with case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations disaggregated by département and commune. PAHO Haiti Country Office also publishes official situation reports citing MSPP data.

PAHO/WHO, UNICEF, UN OCHA, and MSF publish regular Haiti cholera situation reports and humanitarian updates. These sources independently aggregate MSPP data and often provide subnational breakdowns, making them suitable for both collection and validation roles. WHO Disease Outbreak News and the WHO Global Cholera Platform are key validation sources.

Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX), WHO Global Health Observatory, and ECDC may host structured Haiti cholera datasets with time-series case and death counts. These machine-readable sources support cross-validation of extracted records.

Peer-reviewed studies on Haiti cholera epidemiology provide case definitions, count semantics, and methodological context essential for correct interpretation of surveillance data. PubMed, medRxiv, and Lancet Infectious Diseases are key sources.

Haitian news outlets (Le Nouvelliste, AlterPresse, Haiti Libre) and international wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP) may report cholera case counts and deaths citing MSPP or health official statements, providing early signals and corroborating evidence for Q4 2024.
